paragraphs.text: HABITAT RESTORATION TEAM

Help restore and protect Marin’s natural areas from the Marin Headlands to Bolinas Ridge. We’ll explore beautiful park sites while conducting invasive (侵入的) plant removal, winter planting, and seed collection. Habitat Restoration Team volunteers play a vital role in restoring sensitive resources and protecting endangered species across the ridges and valleys.
GROUPS
Groups of five or more require special arrangements and must be confirmed in advance. Please review the List of Available Projects and fill out the Group Project Request Form.
AGE, SKILLS, WHAT TO BRING
Volunteers aged 10 and over are welcome. Read our Youth Policy Guidelines for youth under the age of 15.
Bring your completed Volunteer Agreement Form. Volunteers under the age of 18 must have the parent/guardian approval section signed.
We’ll be working rain or shine. Wear clothes that can get dirty. Bring layers for changing weather and a raincoat if necessary.
Bring a personal water bottle, sunscreen, and lunch.
No experience necessary. Training and tools will be provided. Fulfills (满足) community service requirements.

“I am not crazy,” says Dr. William Farber, shortly after performing acupuncture (针灸) on a rabbit. “I am ahead of my time.” If he seems a little defensive, it might be because even some of his coworkers occasionally laugh at his unusual methods. But Farber is certain he’ll have the last laugh. He’s one of a small but growing number of American veterinarians (兽医) now practicing “holistic” medicine-combining traditional Western treatments with acupuncture, chiropractic (按摩疗法) and herbal medicine.

Farber, a graduate of Colorado State University, started out as a more conventional veterinarian. He became interested in alternative treatments 20 years ago when he suffered from terrible back pain. He tried muscle-relaxing drugs but found little relief. Then he tried acupuncture, an ancient Chinese practice, and was amazed that he improved after two or three treatments. What worked on a veterinarian seemed likely to work on his patients. So, after studying the techniques for a couple of years, he began offering them to pets.

Leigh Tindale’s dog Charlie had a serious heart condition. After Charlie had a heart attack, Tindale says, she was prepared to put him to sleep, but Farber’s treatments eased her dog’s suffering so much that she was able to keep him alive for an additional five months. And Priscilla Dewing reports that her horse, Nappy, “moves more easily and rides more comfortably” after a chiropractic adjustment.

Farber is certain that the holistic approach will grow more popular with time, and if the past is any indication, he may be right: Since 1982, membership in the American Holistic Veterinary Medical Association has grown from 30 to over 700. “Sometimes it surprises me that it works so well,” he says. “I will do anything to help an animal. That’s my job.”

Is comprehension the same whether a person reads a text onscreen or on paper? And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material? The answers to both questions are often “no”. The reasons relate to a variety of factors, including reduced concentration, an entertainment mindset (心态) and a tendency to multitask while consuming digital content.

When reading texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it’s on paper than onscreen. A large amount of research confirms this finding. The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.

The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties. With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages. People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.

But equally important is the mental aspect. Reading researchers have proposed a theory called “shallowing hypothesis (假说) ”. According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.

Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies — say, assigning an online talk instead of an article by the same person. However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.

Digital texts, audio and video all have educational roles, especially when providing resources not available in print. However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.

In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records. Today, most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records. Though they are useful for detecting shifts in the number and variety of species in an area, a new Stanford study has found that this type of record is not perfect.

“With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application,” said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences. “These observations now outnumber the primary data that comes from physical specimens (标本) , and since we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?”
Using a global dataset of 1.9 billion records of plants, insects, birds, and animals, Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns.

“We were particularly interested in exploring the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data, like the greater likelihood of a citizen scientist to take a picture of a flowering plant instead of the grass right next to it,” said Daru.

Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage. Moreover, these data are biased and favor certain regions, time periods, and species. This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby. These data are also biased toward certain species with attractive or eye-catching features.
What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity?

“Quite a lot,” Daru explained. “Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled. To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image.”

paragraphs.text: Not all great writers are great spellers. If you want to be published, it’s vital to submit a perfect, professionally presented manuscript (原稿) .  __36__    No editor is likely to tolerate a writer who does not take the trouble to spell words correctly.

I keep two reference books close-by on my desk: dictionary and thesaurus (同义词词典) . I don’t trust my laptop’s spellchecker.  __37__    Of course, these days there are plenty of online dictionaries and thesauruses, but I’m old-fashioned enough to prefer a hard cover and pages I can leaf through with my fingers. I use the Concise Oxford Dictionary and the Collins Thesaurus.

__38__    It should give you a precise definition of each word, thus differentiating it from other words whose meanings are similar, but not identical. It will also usually show how the word is pronounced.

In addition, I have an old two-volume copy of the Shorter Oxford Dictionary, picked up a few years ago in a bookshop sale for just 99 pence. Of course, with its 2,672 pages, it’s not exactly short. It contains around 163,000 words, plus word combinations and idiomatic phrases.  __39__    However, if I need to check the origin of a word or to look up examples of its usage, there’s nothing better.

For well over a hundred years the most influential English dictionary was Samuel Johnson’s Dictionary of the English Language published in 1755. “To make dictionaries is dull (乏味) work,” wrote Johnson, illustrating one definition of “dull”.  __40__    A few minutes spent casting your eye over a page or two can be a rewarding experience.

Heatherwick Studio recently built a greenhouse at the edge of the National Trust’s Woolbeding Gardens. This beautiful structure, named Glasshouse, is at the centre of a new garden that shows how the Silk Road influences English gardens even in modern times.

The latest  __56__ (engineer) techniques are applied to create this protective  __57__ (function) structure that is also beautiful. The design features ten steel “sepals (萼片) ” made of glass and aluminium (铝) . These sepals open on warm days  __58__ (give) the inside plants sunshine and fresh air. In cold weather, the structure stays  __59__ (close) to protect the plants.

Further, the Silk Route Garden around the greenhouse  __60__ (walk) visitors through a journey influenced by the ancient Silk Road, by which silk as well as many plant species came to Britain for  __61__first time. These plants included modern Western  __62__ (favourite) such as rosemary, lavender and fennel. The garden also contains a winding path that guides visitors through the twelve regions of the Silk Road. The path offers over 300 plant species for visitors to see, too.

假定你是李华，上周五你们班在公园上了一堂美术课。请你给英国朋友Chris写一封邮件分享这次经历，内容包括：
（1）你完成的作品；
（2）你的感想。
（1）写作词数应为80左右；

I met Gunter on a cold, wet and unforgettable evening in September. I had planned to fly to Vienna and take a bus to Prague for a conference. Due to a big storm, my flight had been delayed by an hour and a half. I touched down in Vienna just 30 minutes before the departure of the last bus to Prague. The moment I got off the plane, I ran like crazy through the airport building and jumped into the first taxi on the rank without a second thought.

That was when I met Gunter. I told him where I was going, but he said he hadn’t heard of the bus station. I thought my pronunciation was the problem, so I explained again more slowly, but he still looked confused. When I was about to give up, Gunter fished out his little phone and rang up a friend. After a heated discussion that lasted for what seemed like a century, Gunter put his phone down and started the car.

Finally, with just two minutes to spare we rolled into the bus station. Thankfully, there was a long queue (队列) still waiting to board the bus. Gunter parked the taxi behind the bus, turned around, and looked at me with a big smile on his face. “We made it,” he said.

Just then I realised that I had zero cash in my wallet. I flashed him an apologetic smile as I pulled out my Portuguese bankcard. He tried it several times, but the card machine just did not play along. A feeling of helplessness washed over me as I saw the bus queue thinning out.

At this moment, Gunter pointed towards the waiting hall of the bus station. There, at the entrance, was a cash machine. I jumped out of the car, made a mad run for the machine, and popped my card in, only to read the message: “Out of order. Sorry.”

group-2024-i-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇人物/说明类记叙文，介绍兽医 Dr. William Farber 推行的“holistic” medicine（整体疗法），即把西医传统疗法与针灸、按摩疗法、草药结合。文章通过 Farber 自身经历、宠物病例和协会增长数据，说明这种疗法日益受到认可。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先以 Farber 的自我辩护引出 holistic medicine 及其在美国兽医中的兴起；再追溯他从常规兽医转向替代疗法的个人契机；接着用具体宠物病例佐证疗效；最后用协会会员增长预测该疗法前景并以 Farber 的话收束。

paragraphs.summary: Farber 称自己并非疯狂而是走在时代前面，尽管同事偶尔嘲笑他；他属于日益增多的实践整体疗法的美国兽医之一。
paragraphs.function: 引入人物与核心概念 holistic medicine，并点出他面对的质疑。

paragraphs.summary: Farber 原是常规兽医，二十年前因背痛尝试药物无效后改用针灸，效果显著，于是把针灸用于宠物。
paragraphs.function: 追溯他转向替代疗法的个人原因与契机。

paragraphs.summary: 举例说明疗效：狗 Charlie 的心脏病痛苦得到缓解、多活五个月，马 Nappy 经按摩调理后行动更轻松。
paragraphs.function: 用具体病例例证整体疗法的有效性。

paragraphs.summary: Farber 确信整体疗法会更流行，并以协会会员从30增至700余人为佐证，结尾引用其话语。
paragraphs.function: 用数据支撑其观点并收束全文。

group-2024-i-reading-c.overview: 本文探讨纸质阅读与数字阅读（含音频、视频）在理解与学习效果上的差异，论证纸质阅读在需要深度思考的任务上更有优势，并提醒教育者不要假设所有媒介效果相同。

discourseStructure.summary: 由提问引入主题，先给出总体结论（纸质阅读理解更好），再从物理属性和心理层面两方面解释原因，接着以音频视频为例补充论证，最后落到对教育者的建议。

paragraphs.summary: 提出两个问题：屏幕与纸质阅读理解是否相同，听看内容是否与阅读同样有效，并给出否定回答及原因因素。
paragraphs.function: 提出问题并给出总论点，列举原因因素

paragraphs.summary: 指出长文本在纸上学习通常更成功，尤其在需要心理抽象的任务上纸质优势更突出。
paragraphs.function: 给出研究结论，强调纸质阅读优势

paragraphs.summary: 从纸张物理属性角度解释差异：触感、页面视觉地理及与记忆位置的关联。
paragraphs.function: 解释原因之一：物理属性

paragraphs.summary: 从心理层面解释差异，介绍“浅化假说”：人们用社交媒体心态对待数字文本，投入更少脑力。
paragraphs.function: 解释原因之二：心理层面

paragraphs.summary: 音频视频比文本更吸引人，教师日益采用，但心理学研究表明阅读新闻比听看记得更多。
paragraphs.function: 补充论证：音视频虽吸引人但记忆效果不如阅读

paragraphs.summary: 承认数字文本、音视频有教育作用，但在需要专注与反思的学习中，提醒教育者勿假设所有媒介相同。
paragraphs.function: 总结并给出建议

group-2024-i-reading-d.overview: 本文是一篇科普说明文，介绍斯坦福大学一项关于生物多样性记录的研究。文章指出如今的生物多样性记录多为照片、视频等数字观察数据，虽便于收集，但研究发现这类观察数据存在偏差，并给出改进建议。

discourseStructure.summary: 文章先提出当今生物多样性记录多以数字形式存在但并不完美（提出问题），接着引出研究者 Daru 及其研究问题——观察数据是否可用，然后说明研究方法与关注的偏差来源，再揭示研究结论（观察数据存在偏差且偏向特定区域、时段和物种），最后给出对生物多样性应用的改进建议。

paragraphs.summary: 如今大多数生物多样性记录以照片、视频等数字形式存在，虽有助于监测物种变化，但斯坦福研究发现这类记录并不完美。
paragraphs.function: 引入话题并提出问题：数字观察记录并不完美。

paragraphs.summary: 研究主导者 Daru 指出借助移动应用进行物种观察变得容易，这些观察数据已超过实体标本的原始数据，他想知道这些数据是否可用。
paragraphs.function: 引出研究者及其核心研究问题。

paragraphs.summary: Daru 团队使用19亿条植物、昆虫、鸟类和动物记录，检验这些数据对实际全球生物多样性格局的代表程度。
paragraphs.function: 说明研究的数据规模与方法。

paragraphs.summary: Daru 表示团队特别关注会使数据产生偏差的采样因素，如公民科学家更可能拍摄开花植物而非旁边的草。
paragraphs.function: 进一步说明研究关注的偏差来源——采样方式。

paragraphs.summary: 研究发现大量纯观察记录并未带来更好的全球覆盖，反而偏向特定区域、时段和物种，因为公民科学家多在附近区域记录，且偏好有吸引力的物种。
paragraphs.function: 揭示研究结论：观察数据存在偏差。

paragraphs.summary: 以设问形式引出：面对不完美的生物多样性数据集我们能做什么。
paragraphs.function: 过渡设问，引出解决方案。

paragraphs.summary: Daru 给出建议：应用可利用研究结果引导用户去采样不足的地区与物种，并鼓励用户请专家确认所上传图像的识别。
paragraphs.function: 给出对生物多样性应用的改进建议。

locationParaphrases.note: 选项 treat ... lightly 同义替换原文 not so serious 且 devote less mental effort，对应读者轻率对待数字文本。

q-2024-i-030.questionFocus: 考查大学教师日益使用音频视频原因的细节理解。
q-2024-i-030.stemTranslationZh: 为什么大学教师越来越多地使用音频和视频？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们能抓住学生的注意力。

evidence.quote: Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies
evidence.anchor: 音视频更吸引人，故教师日益采用

trap.claim: 教师使用音视频是因为准备起来更方便
trap.explanation: 原文给出的原因是 more engaging（更吸引人），未提及“准备方便”，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们有助于培养高级技能。

trap.claim: 教师使用音视频是因为它们有助于培养高级技能
trap.explanation: 原文恰恰指出阅读在需心理抽象的高级任务上更好，并未说音视频培养高级技能，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们比文本提供更多信息。

trap.sourceText: Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text
trap.optionText: They are more informative than text.
trap.relationNote: 选项借用原文 more ... than text 句式，把 more engaging（更吸引人）偷换成 more informative（信息更多），原文并未说音视频信息量更大。

trapEvidence.quote: Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text
trapEvidence.anchor: more engaging 而非 more informative

locationParaphrases.targetText: Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies
locationParaphrases.note: 选项 hold students' attention 同义替换原文 more engaging（更吸引人），and so 揭示因果，即教师采用音视频的原因。

q-2024-i-031.questionFocus: 考查对最后一段作者言外之意的推断。
q-2024-i-031.stemTranslationZh: 作者在最后一段暗示了什么？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 学生应该运用多种学习技巧。

trap.sourceQuote: educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same
trap.optionText: Students should apply multiple learning techniques.
trap.explanation: 原文建议的对象是 educators（教育者），而非 students；且讨论的是媒介选择而非学生运用多种学习技巧，对象与内容均错配。

trapEvidence.quote: educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same
trapEvidence.anchor: 建议对象是 educators 而非 students

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 教师应该制作自己的教学材料。

trap.claim: 教师应该制作自己的教学材料
trap.explanation: 原文只建议教育者不要假设所有媒介相同，从未提及教师“自制教学材料”，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 印刷文本在教育中无法被完全取代。

evidence.quote: for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.
evidence.anchor: 需专注反思时不应认为各媒介相同

evidence.quote: Digital texts, audio and video all have educational roles, especially when providing resources not available in print.
evidence.anchor: 数字媒介有作用但纸质仍不可替代

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 课堂之外的教育不容忽视。

trap.claim: 课堂之外的教育不容忽视
trap.explanation: 末段讨论的是不同媒介的学习效果差异，并未涉及“课堂内外”教育的问题，属无中生有。

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Print texts cannot be entirely replaced in education.
locationParaphrases.targetText: for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.
locationParaphrases.note: 由 shouldn’t assume all media are the same 加上 maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for，可推断在需深度学习时纸质文本不可被完全取代。

q-2024-i-032.questionFocus: 考查对第一段中关于当今物种记录形式这一细节的理解。
q-2024-i-032.stemTranslationZh: 关于如今收集到的物种记录，我们了解到什么？

trap.claim: 如今的物种记录正在变得过时。
trap.explanation: 原文未提及记录过时（outdated）的内容，文章只说这类数字记录并不完美，并未说它们正在过时，属无中生有。

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它们大多以电子形式存在。

evidence.quote: most records of biodiversity are often in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records
evidence.anchor: 记录多为照片、视频等数字形式

trap.sourceQuote: researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records
trap.explanation: 原文说已收集到数十亿条记录（billions of records），数量庞大，选项却说数量有限（limited in number），与原文趋势相反，属黑白颠倒。

trapEvidence.quote: researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records

trap.claim: 这些记录被用于公开展览。
trap.explanation: 原文说这些记录用于监测某地区物种数量与种类的变化，并未提及用于公开展览（public exhibition），属无中生有。

locationParaphrases.targetText: in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records
locationParaphrases.note: 选项的 in electronic form 是原文 digital records（photos, videos, and other digital records）的同义替换，digital 与 electronic 对应。

q-2024-i-033.questionFocus: 考查对 Daru 研究对象（聚焦于何种数据）这一细节的把握。
q-2024-i-033.stemTranslationZh: Daru 的研究聚焦于什么？

trap.claim: Daru 的研究聚焦于受威胁的物种。
trap.explanation: 首段虽提到物种灭绝（go extinct）的背景，但研究本身聚焦的是观察数据是否可用，并未以受威胁物种为研究对象，属无中生有。

trap.sourceText: the primary data that comes from physical specimens
trap.relationNote: 原文出现 physical specimens 一词，但只是作为对照（观察数据已超过来自实体标本的原始数据），研究聚焦的是观察数据而非实体标本，选项借原词设钩干扰。

trapEvidence.quote: These observations now outnumber the primary data that comes from physical specimens
trapEvidence.anchor: 观察数据已超过实体标本数据

evidence.quote: since we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?
evidence.anchor: 想知道观察数据是否可用

evidence.quote: Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns
evidence.anchor: 检验这些数据的代表性

trap.sourceText: make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application
trap.relationNote: 原文提到 mobile application 只是说明人们借助它进行观察的手段，研究聚焦的是由此产生的观察数据，而非移动应用本身，选项借原词设钩干扰。

trapEvidence.quote: it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application
trapEvidence.anchor: 借助移动应用进行观察

locationParaphrases.targetText: we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?
locationParaphrases.note: 题干问研究 focus on 什么，原文以 Daru 自述 I wanted to know: Are they usable? 直接点明研究对象为 observational data，正确选项与原文用词一致。

q-2024-i-034.questionFocus: 考查对造成数据偏差原因这一细节的理解，需结合采样方式定位。
q-2024-i-034.stemTranslationZh: 根据这项研究，是什么导致了偏差？

trap.claim: 偏差是由数据分析中的错误造成的。
trap.explanation: 原文将偏差归因于采样（sampling）方式，并未提及数据分析中的错误，属无中生有。

trap.claim: 偏差是由上传图片质量差造成的。
trap.explanation: 末段提到请专家确认上传图像的识别是为提高数据质量，但原文从未把偏差归因于图片质量差，属无中生有。

evidence.quote: We were particularly interested in exploring the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data, like the greater likelihood of a citizen scientist to take a picture of a flowering plant instead of the grass right next to it
evidence.anchor: 采样方式使数据产生偏差

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 不可靠的数据采集设备。

trap.claim: 偏差是由不可靠的数据采集设备造成的。
trap.explanation: 原文提到 mobile devices 只是说明公民科学家用移动设备记录，偏差源于采样行为而非设备不可靠，原文未提及设备不可靠，属无中生有。

locationParaphrases.targetText: the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data
locationParaphrases.note: 题干问 led to the biases 的原因，原文 aspects of sampling that tend to bias data 指出采样的某些方面导致偏差，正确选项 Improper way of sampling 是对其的同义概括。

q-2024-i-035.questionFocus: 考查对末段 Daru 针对生物多样性应用提出的建议这一细节的理解。
q-2024-i-035.stemTranslationZh: Daru 对生物多样性应用有什么建议？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 审查来自特定区域的数据。

trap.sourceQuote: Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
trap.sourceHighlight: lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled
trap.explanation: 原文建议是告知用户过度采样区域并引导其前往采样不足的地方，而非审查（review）特定区域的数据，选项偷换了建议的具体内容。

trapEvidence.quote: Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
trapEvidence.anchor: 引导用户前往采样不足之处

trap.sourceQuote: biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image
trap.sourceEntity: users (encouraged to have an expert confirm)
trap.optionText: Hire experts to check the records.
trap.explanation: 原文是应用鼓励用户去请专家确认上传图像，动作主体与方式是用户主动求证；选项却说雇佣专家核查记录，把对象与做法错配。

trapEvidence.quote: biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image

trap.sourceQuote: encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image
trap.optionText: Confirm the identity of the users.
trap.explanation: 原文 confirm the identification 指确认上传图像（物种）的识别，选项却理解为确认用户的身份（identity of the users），将确认对象由图像识别错配为用户身份。

trapEvidence.quote: encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 为公民科学家提供指导。

evidence.quote: Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
evidence.anchor: 告知用户并引导前往采样不足之处

evidence.quote: the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists
evidence.anchor: 这些用户即公民科学家

locationParaphrases.targetText: inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled
locationParaphrases.note: 正确选项 Give guidance 是原文 inform users... and lead them to places 的同义替换；结合第五段 users 即 citizen scientists，可知指导对象为公民科学家。
